generation_defaults.single_photograph: One physically possible real or documentary photograph. A photographed laboratory setup is allowed when honestly identified; no diagrams, collages, animation, or artificial optical overlays.
generation_defaults.prompt_scope: Describe causal scene conditions and the intended phenomenon, not the predicted optical answer. Generate independent scenes without evaluation examples or scoring rubrics.
generation_defaults.hidden_check: Exactly one short observable optical check is auxiliary metadata, separate from the user request and exported training prompt.
generation_defaults.classification: Choose the dominant intended physical phenomenon and record one listed subphenomenon. Neighboring effects may coexist but must not replace the target.

categories.name_zh: 双折射与窗体应力彩纹
includes: Polarization-dependent stress or layer anisotropy in transparent glazing and polymer materials.
Photographable photoelastic color or intensity patterns under suitable illumination and analysis.
excludes: Uniform tint, colored scene reflections, paint and unsupported rainbow patterns in bare transparent material.
A calcite double image alone as a substitute for the stress-pattern subphenomena of this category.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Specify a plausible birefringent or stressed transparent material and suitable polarization conditions.
Patterns need not universally be straight, smooth, monochromatic or free of swirls; appearance depends on stress, thickness and polarization.
Do not copy a desired pattern into the user prompt or treat a particular artistic pattern as a universal optical law.

includes: Concentrated light networks, curves or cusps on a receiving surface after refraction or curved-surface reflection.
excludes: Surface glints aimed at the camera, aperture light patches, printed patterns and self-emission.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Include a feasible source, shaping surface and receiver.
Caustics need not be colored; bright surface reflection alone does not establish focusing onto a receiver.

includes: Compact diffraction rings close to the apparent Sun, Moon or another source through small droplets.
excludes: Antisolar glories, large ice halos, lens ghosts and the solar plasma corona.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Place the phenomenon around the viewed light source with a plausible thin droplet layer.
Do not use an observer shadow to identify a source-centered corona.

includes: Convex or concave mirror images whose scale or deformation depends on surface shape and object position.
Real object images formed by concave mirrors on a receiver.
excludes: Lens refraction, full-frame fisheye projection and bright caustics without object imaging.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Make the reflective surface and reference object identifiable.
Specify feasible object and viewing placement without prescribing image orientation or size.

includes: Spikes around source images caused by aperture edges, slits or telescope support structures.
excludes: Actual rays through scattering media, off-source lens ghosts, sensor blooming and decorative light patterns.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Specify a compact source and a relevant optical aperture or obstruction.
Spike count alone does not uniquely determine a physical blade count.

includes: Wavelength-dependent refraction separating or redirecting different colors.
excludes: Water-drop rainbows, grating spectra, thin-film interference, absorption coloring and lens color fringes alone.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Specify a suitable transparent dispersive medium, source spectrum and observable transmitted path or receiver.
Do not prescribe the resulting color order or angular displacement in the user request.

includes: Selective focus, foreground or background defocus, bokeh and tilted focus planes.
excludes: A generically sharp photograph, motion smear, fog attenuation, translucent scattering and heat distortion.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Specify the intended focus target and meaningful scene depth without prescribing the evaluated optical result.
Keep defocus separate from exposure-time motion effects.

includes: Barrel, pincushion and fisheye image mapping with visible geometric references.
excludes: Perspective convergence, naturally curved objects, local vessel refraction and turbulent warping.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Provide identifiable lines or spatial structure and an appropriate optical system.
A wide-angle view need not have barrel distortion; do not equate perspective with lens distortion.

includes: Diffraction orders, spectra or spot patterns produced by periodic grooves, slits or grids.
excludes: Thin-film color, prism dispersion, printed color and sensor sampling moire.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Identify a plausible periodic structure and source spectrum.
Do not prescribe color ordering, order spacing or a uniform full rainbow across every part of the surface.

includes: Low-altitude solar or lunar disk deformation, atmospheric color rims, green flashes and celestial mirages.
excludes: An ordinary orange sunset without refractive disk features, size illusion and off-disk lens ghosts.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Use a low-altitude celestial source and plausible atmospheric layering.
A single photograph can record a visible rim feature but cannot establish its duration or time evolution.

includes: Ice-crystal halo rings and partial arcs around the Sun or Moon.
excludes: Small droplet diffraction coronas, parhelia and oriented crystal arcs as the primary subject, and lens ring ghosts.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Provide appropriate high ice clouds and source geometry.
Cloud coverage can interrupt a halo; do not force a complete uniform circle.

categories.name_en: Total internal reflection and Snell windows
includes: Total internal reflection at high-to-low refractive-index interfaces.
Underwater Snell-window views and internally guided light.
excludes: Air-side reflections on water, circular frames and wide-angle skies without the required interface geometry.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Light must reach the boundary from the higher-index medium under appropriate incidence conditions.
Outside a Snell window the observer can still see reflected underwater surroundings.

includes: Lens-internal ghost images, aperture-shaped stray patches and veiling glare from strong illumination.
excludes: Scene reflections, volume light shafts, droplet coronas, bokeh and aperture diffraction spikes alone.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Specify a feasible strong-light direction relative to the camera and a scene that supports inspecting stray light.
Do not invent physical objects or emitted beams to explain lens artifacts.

includes: Virtual imaging through positive magnifiers within the focal range and negative spectacle lenses.
excludes: Real images projected onto a screen, compound microscopes or telescopes, and ordinary curved vessels.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Specify a plausible lens type and object placement while leaving the resulting scale and orientation to optical reasoning.

includes: Vertical-looking bands caused by reflection from suitably oriented atmospheric ice crystals.
excludes: Searchlight beams, aurora, sensor smear and elongated reflections on water.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Specify a plausible ice-crystal environment and light source.
Pillars are an apparent reflection geometry, not literal upward columns of emitted light.

categories.name_zh: 长曝光、运动模糊与闪光拖尾
categories.name_en: Long exposure, motion blur and flash trails
includes: Photographable exposure-time integration of moving subjects, light sources or fluids.
Relative camera tracking and subject motion, and flash-frozen detail combined with ambient exposure trails.
excludes: Defocus alone, atmospheric turbulence, repeated-image composites, animation and digitally drawn motion lines.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Use one continuous, physically plausible exposure and specify camera support or tracking when it matters.
Flash trails require both a brief flash contribution and ambient exposure; do not demand a flash effect without suitable light.
Do not prescribe the resulting blur direction or path; leave it to the actual camera and subject motion.
Long exposure need not blur stationary objects, and camera tracking does not make every subject part equally sharp.

includes: Cloud or fog droplet scattering, forward glow and loss of contrast through a droplet-filled path.
excludes: Defocused point lights, lens contamination, white solid surfaces and resolved diffraction coronas.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Make the atmospheric medium and its illumination evident; do not substitute camera blur for fog.

includes: Atmospheric refractive layering that produces displaced, inverted, stacked or stretched distant-object images.
excludes: Real water reflections, local random heat distortion alone and anomalous solar or lunar disks.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Supply plausible thermal layering and a sufficiently distant reference object.
Separate a stable layered mirage from turbulent shimmer, although both may coexist.

includes: Successive reflections between distinct mirrors, recursive images, angled-mirror repetitions and folded viewing paths.
excludes: Two coplanar mirrors alone, copied objects, screens, multiple shadows and lens ghosts.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Specify which surfaces take part in successive reflections.
Do not equate visible image count with a universal formula when field of view or occlusion changes.

includes: Apparent displacement or deformation across refractive interfaces, submerged-object depth and curved transparent vessels.
Visible interface refraction and parallel-slab displacement.
excludes: Ordinary surface reflection, dedicated virtual-image lenses and total internal reflection as the main effect.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Identify the relevant transparent media, interface and reference object.
A curved vessel can have different imaging behavior in different directions; do not impose a universal inversion or magnification.

includes: Compact colored rings around the antisolar direction in cloud or mist.
Brocken shadow projections on cloud or mist, including cases without resolved colored rings.
excludes: Source-centered coronas, broad fogbows and ordinary shadows on a solid surface.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Put the illumination behind the observer relative to the cloud or mist screen.
Label a shadow-only Brocken scene separately; a shadow alone does not establish colored glory rings.

includes: Parhelia, circumzenithal arcs and circumhorizontal arcs produced by oriented ice crystals.
excludes: Arbitrary colored clouds, ordinary rainbows, complete halo rings alone and vertical light pillars.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Choose solar elevation and crystal conditions appropriate to the intended subphenomenon.
Do not force paired parhelia, equal brightness or a generic arc location shared by all subtypes.

categories.name_zh: 颗粒散射与丁达尔效应
includes: Particles or colloids making an illuminated path visible within a scattering medium.
excludes: Glass-surface highlights, visible apparatus without a scattering path, and generic blue sky.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Identify the particles or suspension and a feasible illumination path.
Use this category when the medium and local scattering are central; use volumetric for the spatial beam or shadow geometry.

includes: Recognizable virtual images in a planar mirror with object identity, viewpoint and occlusion relationships.
Separate coplanar mirror fragments showing parts of the same view.
excludes: Ordinary water or glossy-surface reflections without an explicit planar mirror.
Successive reflections between different mirrors and curved-mirror imaging.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Use one coherent viewpoint and specify the mirror plane, real objects and relevant occluders.
Do not prescribe a reflected pose or assume screen-space left-right reversal without geometry.

includes: Primary bows formed by illuminated rain, spray or water droplets, including partial and circular views.
excludes: Solar-side ice halos, small observer-centered glories, prism spectra and colored artificial overlays.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Arrange the observer, source and droplet region plausibly.
Do not require a complete arc when droplets or the field of view cover only a portion.

includes: Short-wavelength atmospheric scattering, long-path sky color and distance-dependent aerial perspective.
excludes: Blue object pigment, arbitrary color grading, shallow focus and dense white fog alone.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Provide atmospheric illumination or distance context; a blue background alone is not evidence.
Avoid claiming a scattering mechanism solely from a material color.

categories.name_zh: 反射虹、倒影虹与高阶虹
includes: Rainbows formed with sunlight first reflected by a water surface.
Rainbows seen as reflections in water.
Third- and fourth-order droplet rainbows, including photographable controlled droplet effects.
excludes: Generic water reflections, supernumerary fringes, ordinary double rainbows and lens ghosts.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Distinguish reflection before rainbow formation from reflection of the already formed rainbow.
Higher-order bows require their own droplet and source-view geometry; a water mirror is not evidence of higher order.
Do not prescribe a guaranteed strong visible bow when the scene lacks enough contrast or droplet extent.

includes: Passive materials returning illumination preferentially toward the source, observed near the illumination axis.
excludes: Ordinary specular highlights, self-emitting lamps, LEDs and fluorescent color alone.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Provide plausible near-observer illumination and a distinguishable passive reflective material.
Do not require every surface to brighten identically or reinterpret reflective material as a light source.

includes: Secondary bows, primary-secondary pairs and the darker region between them.
excludes: Fine supernumerary fringes, water reflections of a primary bow and bows caused by a separate reflected light source.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Specify rain or spray and plausible source-observer geometry.
Do not prescribe color reversal, relative radius or uniform visibility in the user prompt.

categories.name_zh: 光源与阴影、自然孔隙投影
categories.name_en: Single-source shadows and natural aperture projections
includes: Shadows and penumbrae from one dominant light source or directional sunlight.
Natural small apertures projecting the solar disk, including partial-eclipse illumination.
excludes: Multiple independently positioned lights and colored multi-source shadows.
Transmission coloring, caustics, or indoor camera-obscura street images.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Specify the source, occluder and receiving surface sufficiently to support a visible shadow relationship.
An aperture projection is a bright source image, not necessarily the shape of the opening.
Do not infer metric shadow bearings from uncalibrated image pixels.

includes: Material-dependent colored transmission and light attenuation on a receiving surface.
Diffused silhouettes through translucent materials.
excludes: Colored shadows caused by blocking separate colored lamps.
Opaque painted color, defocus, and concentrated caustic light patterns.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Describe the transmitting material, illumination and receiver; do not assign emitted light to a passive sheet.

includes: Narrow supernumerary interference fringes associated with a rainbow.
Broad weakly colored bows formed by small fog droplets.
excludes: Secondary bows, reflection bows, higher-order bows and compact glories.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Describe a physically suitable droplet environment and viewing geometry.
Treat supernumerary fringes and fogbows as separate subphenomena rather than a generic rare-rainbow bucket.

includes: Color and reflective appearance produced by natural biological or material microstructure.
excludes: Painted coloration alone, colored spotlights, broad thin-film patches and periodic optical gratings as the main subject.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Use a physically plausible species or material and ordinary illumination.
A single image may show spatial angle dependence but cannot prove temporal color change.
Retain the visible structure and material boundaries rather than replacing the subject with a luminous color overlay.

includes: Water, wet ground, glazing and material-dependent specular or rough-surface reflection.
Visible redirection of light by a reflecting surface.
excludes: Explicit planar or curved mirror object imaging as the main effect.
Underwater objects seen by transmission, retroreflection, and focused patterns on a separate receiver.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Distinguish the reflected scene from a transmitted view and from a highlight.
Specify a source and a visible scattering medium when a light path itself must be visible.

includes: Interference color or intensity structure from thin films in reflection or transmission.
excludes: Paint, colored illumination, ordinary colored reflections, grating spectra and prism dispersion.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Specify a physically plausible thin film and illumination/viewing context.
Keep optical patterns tied to the film extent; film shape alone does not establish interference.

includes: Local image deformation or degradation caused by fluctuating air refractive index.
Photographable astronomical seeing or speckle structure when the capture conditions support it.
excludes: Ordinary defocus, motion blur, stable lens distortion and claims of temporal scintillation from one isolated static star.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Use spatial detail or reference edges that make atmospheric distortion observable.
A single image cannot demonstrate rapid temporal variation; do not request animation or multi-frame panels to evade the single-photograph format.
Keep layered mirage imaging distinct from random turbulent deformation.

includes: Spatial light shafts, light sheets and volumetric shadows in scattering air or water.
excludes: Only a bright patch on a solid surface, ice-crystal light pillars and camera diffraction spikes.
physical_constraints: Use one physically possible camera view in a single real or documentary photograph; no diagrams, collages, or synthetic overlays.
Specify causal illumination, material, placement and viewing conditions; keep predicted optical answers out of the user prompt.
Specify a scattering medium and plausible source or occluding aperture.
Perspective convergence is not proof that physically parallel shafts meet at a nearby point.
